neighbours.label: the preposition after a parent's mention of their child (my daughter is in / pick my son up from / the kids are home from), where school is the expected continuation; the same frames with an adult subject stay low
fire: We moved last spring, and now my son is in a new school near the river.
Our youngest is in fourth grade this year and loves his teacher.
On Fridays I leave work early to pick my daughter up from practice.
Now that both of our girls are in college, the house feels very quiet.
My twins went back to class on Monday after the long holiday.
Her son is in kindergarten, so she can only work mornings.
When the kids are home from school, the kitchen turns into chaos.
I drop my little boy off at daycare before catching the bus.
quiet: We moved last spring, and now my brother is in a new office near the river.
Our manager is in Berlin this week and loves the conference.
On Fridays I leave work early to pick my car up from the garage.
Now that both of our tenants are in Spain, the house feels very quiet.
My colleagues went back to the office on Monday after the long holiday.
Her husband is in the navy, so she can only travel in summer.
When the guests are back from the beach, the kitchen turns into chaos.
I drop my laptop off at the repair shop before catching the bus.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.5 on in/from/to after a child subject, whatever follows; adult-subject rewrites below 0.1
short: preposition after a child subject, predicting school
notes: Card: ' to' x5, ' in' x4, ' from' x3, ' at' x3 after child subjects, mostly before 'school/college'. Probe: 'My daughter is in high school' 0.490 and 'My daughter is in the kitchen' 0.490 (identical: the setup fires, not the destination), 'kids are in college' 0.458, 'pick my son up from school' 0.306; 'engineers are in a meeting' 0.017, 'walked to the station' 0.012.
